answer: A guarantor orchard blocks fake identities. Each guarantor may vouch for eight agents, each locking 40 units in a vault. Auditors sample vouched work; a fake forfeits its 40 units and halves the guarantor's quota. The k-th fake costs a guarantor slot plus 40 units, growing with n because guarantors are scarce and slashed slots cannot be reused; auditors enforce the forfeit. Renting a guarantor fails because a slash wipes its orchard. For 1,000 fakes that is 40,000 units plus 125 guarantors, while one honest agent pays 40 units and keeps a ferrous bond with its guarantor.
